You are the whole team, and a website is not your job

Run a one-person business and the math is brutal: every hour spent wrestling with a website builder is an hour not spent on the product, the client, or the next sale. You are the founder, the fulfillment department, the support line, and the marketing team, all in the same body. Hiring a developer to build a five-page site is a real, ongoing cost for an operation with one name on the invoice, and most freelance quotes assume you have a team to manage the back-and-forth. You do not have that time either.

So the site gets pushed to next quarter. Or you settle for a drag-and-drop template that looks like every other template, because finishing beats perfect. Neither outcome is good enough when your website is often the first, and sometimes only, impression a potential customer gets of your business.

How Kodely fits into a one-person operation

Kodely skips the parts of web development that used to require a second person. You describe your business in plain English in a chat interface, and Kodely generates a real Vite plus React 19 plus TypeScript plus Tailwind CSS v4 application, actual component files, not a static mockup. You watch the live preview render the real compiled app as it is built, so there is no gap between what you asked for and what you can see.

A one-page site for a digital product or service

A personal-brand site for a creator

Your audience lives across two or three platforms and there is no single place that is unmistakably yours. A personal site ties it together: bio, links to your work, a content archive, a way to get in touch. Describe your niche and what you want visitors to do first, and iterate from there without touching a line of code yourself.

A booking-inquiry page for a solo service provider

Consultants, coaches, photographers, and other solo service providers mainly need one job done well: explain what you offer and make it effortless for someone to ask about booking you.
